content.summary: Three constructive checks support the existing guarded formulations against Beta’s concerns. The rho partition preserves the wider-support case, trace refinement preserves multiplicities, and the direct A3 argument proves positivity in the required order. No additional manuscript repair follows. These checks do not establish every model row or imported theorem.

findings.statement: Multiplicity-preserving refinement supports the projection interface, with shared-builder dependence retained.
findings.disposition: Counting identities do not prove equivalence of complete LPs or validate every strengthening row.

findings.statement: The separate rho domains remain necessary for complete coverage.
findings.disposition: The wider-support rho 8 control belongs to its own branch; neither the eleven-point reduction nor R16-minus-one classification is extended to it.

findings.statement: The exact H27 input remains indispensable to the current positivity argument.
findings.disposition: The parameterized identity explains sensitivity without repairing external provenance or proving H27 locally.

revisions.action: Tested coarse-to-fine trace aggregation against the implemented boxes and incidence rows.
revisions.result: Selected-marker refinement preserves the actual-family counting interpretation.

revisions.action: Checked Beta’s counterexample against the exact rho partition and classification proof.
revisions.result: The retained guard excludes the invalid extension; no broader classification is needed.

revisions.action: Derived the general A3 positivity bound and compared the source ordering.
revisions.result: H27 remains explicit and quantitatively essential to this argument.

checks.scope: Guarded rho partition as the constructive alternative to overclassification
checks.method: Read LOW15-R15-rho7-classification.md and the prior H2 shape argument at main.tex:584–611; checked Beta’s literal rho 8 control.
checks.observation: The control has 15 members, support 13 and rho 8. Exact-rho7 classification chooses an actual seven-disjoint anchor and separately analyzes one/two uv-triples; it does not copy the prior size 16 conclusion. Sections 5.2–6 correctly reserve support 11 for rho<=6 and use the separate cover route at rho 8. A finite tree replay cannot replace these guards.

checks.method: Read degree19_projection_v5.py:68–98 and D19-model-bridge.md Section 2; independently checked trace aggregation and incidence indicators.
checks.observation: Beta’s two-completion example refines from coarse count 2 to proper count 1 plus full-four count 1. All 1093 fine trace types map to the 794 coarse types, and 325714 incidence comparisons commute with restriction. The source retains proper-triple upper 2, full-four upper 1 and the combined triple-incidence row. This verifies a counting interface, not feasibility of a size 68 model.

checks.scope: Direct Jin repair with an explicit positivity interface
checks.method: Read LOW15-direct-Jin-A3-addon.md and independently checked its cyclic coefficient identities with n and independence cap h left symbolic.
checks.observation: From sum(b)=3n and b_i<=h, the inverse identity gives a_i>=2n-5h. At n=68 this is 1 for h=27 and -4 for h=28. The source establishes positivity before b_i>=25 and retains strict Jin inequality 275>272, yielding the same later fibre domain without an empty-fibre reduction. Bounded scripts/results are preserved in checks/round08/methodologist/.
